text: When a family returns food or medication, the money should go back the way it came: to the card first, then to their account for the credit part.
Open the paid bill. Maria paid it with her card and some account credit.
Return the items, and Scout works out where the money goes.
Click Return items.
Scout shows how the bill was paid, and how much the card can still take.
Type 1 to return one bag.
It goes back on the shelf, and the amount fits on the card, so it all goes back to the card.
Click refund.
Scout asks once more.
Confirm.
The bill stays paid. The return is its own line.
Now the other bag. Click Return items again.
Scout only offers what's left to return, and the card has only a little left.
Type 1 for the second bag.
That's more than the card has left, so the rest goes back as account credit.
Click refund.
Read the split.
Then confirm.
Both payments show as refunded, not voided, and Maria has her credit back.
If the family would rather keep it all as credit, use Keep as account credit instead.

The most common mistakes are refunding the whole amount to the card when part was paid with credit, and doing a plain refund when items came back. Use Return items, so stock and the chart are right. Remember: return the items, and Scout works out the split.
